title: Understanding Datasets, Data Points, Features, and Labels
introduction: In machine learning we need data. This lesson explains the basic parts of data – datasets, records, rows, columns, features, and labels – and how they help a model learn.

sections.heading: What Is a Dataset?
sections.subheading: A collection of data used for learning
paragraphs: A dataset is a group of related data that we use to train or test a machine‑learning model.
It can be stored in a table, a spreadsheet, or a file, and it contains many rows and columns.

example.title: Student Grades Dataset
example.content: A table that lists each student, the number of hours they studied, their attendance, and their final exam score.

sections.heading: Data Points, Records, Rows, and Columns
sections.subheading: How individual pieces of data are organized
paragraphs: Each row in a dataset is called a data point, record, or instance. It represents one observation.
Columns are the attributes of the data. Each column holds the same type of information for all rows.

example.title: One Student’s Record
example.content: Row: {Student ID: 101, Hours Studied: 5, Attendance: 90%, Final Score: 78}.

sections.heading: Features – The Input Variables
paragraphs: Features are the columns that we give to the model as input. They describe the characteristics of each data point.
Good features help the model learn patterns that lead to accurate predictions.

example.title: Features in the Grades Dataset
example.content: Hours Studied and Attendance are features because they are used to predict the final score.

sections.heading: Labels and Targets – The Output Variables
sections.subheading: What the model tries to predict
paragraphs: A label (also called a target) is the column that contains the answer we want the model to learn.
During training the model compares its predictions to the true labels and adjusts itself.

example.title: Label in the Grades Dataset
example.content: Final Score is the label because the model aims to predict this value from the features.

practice.title: Identify Features and Label
practice.instruction:
Look at the table below and write down which columns are features and which column is the label:
Student ID | Hours Studied | Attendance | Final Score

keyTakeaways: A dataset is a collection of rows (data points) and columns (attributes) used for machine learning.
Features are input columns that describe each data point; labels are the output column the model predicts.
Understanding the difference between inputs (features) and targets (labels) is essential for building a good model.

mcqs.question: What best describes a dataset in machine learning?
options: A collection of rows and columns used for training or testing a model
A single data point that the model predicts
The algorithm that updates model parameters
A programming language for data analysis
mcqs.explanation: A dataset is the whole table of data, containing many rows (data points) and columns (attributes), that we use to train or evaluate a model.

mcqs.question: In a dataset, each row is also called a:
mcqs.explanation: Every row represents one observation and is referred to as a data point, record, or instance.

mcqs.question: Which columns are features in the Student Grades dataset?
mcqs.explanation: Features are the input variables used for prediction; in this example they are Hours Studied and Attendance.

mcqs.question: What is the label (target) in the Student Grades dataset?
mcqs.explanation: The label is the column the model tries to predict, which is the Final Score in this dataset.

mcqs.question: Why are good features important for a machine‑learning model?
options: They increase the size of the dataset
They are the values the model predicts
They are not used during training
They help the model learn patterns for accurate predictions
mcqs.explanation: Good features provide useful information that allows the model to discover patterns and make accurate predictions.
